title: Alvarez: complete and incomplete sufficiency
source_text: XXIX. Quippe ut notat Alvarez, duplex est Auxilium ad operationem aliquam sufficiens. Unum est enim complete sufficiens, nimirum ultra quod nullum aliud auxilium est absolute necessarium, ut illa operatio actu producatur. Alterum non complete quidem, sed tamen vere sufficiens est, quod, scilicet, tribuit posse comparatione ejusdem operationis: ita ut nullum aliud auxilium sit absolute necessarium, ut homo vere dicatur posse operationem illam producere: quemadmodum ut dicatur homo posse videre, non aliud requiritur quam ut habeat potentiam Visivam: quanquam ultra potentiam Visivam, alia plura requirantur ut aliquis actu videat. Et in hoc sensu asserit, per auxilia gratiae, quam sufficientem vocat, vere posse hominem operari actum illum, comparatione cujus dicitur sufficiens; etiamsi nunquam sit operaturus, nisi Deus auxilio efficaci efficiat, ut illa reducatur ad actum secundum. Atque sic auxilium ad credendum sufficiens est illud, quo potest homo credere: & auxilium sufficiens ad perseverandum illud, quo potest perseverare si velit: quanquam ut sit voliturus, requiratur praeterea auxilium efficax. Epit. de auxiliis divinae gratiae lib. 3. cap. 17.
pass_a_gloss: XXIX. For as Alvarez notes, the Help sufficient for some operation is twofold. For one is completely sufficient, namely beyond which no other help is absolutely necessary, that that operation be produced in act. The other not completely indeed, but yet truly sufficient, which, namely, gives being able in comparison with the same operation: so that no other help is absolutely necessary, that man may truly be said to be able to produce that operation: just as that man be said to be able to see, nothing else is required than that he have the Visive power: although beyond the Visive power, several other things are required that someone see in act. And in this sense he asserts, that through the helps of grace, which he calls sufficient, man can truly work that act, in comparison with which it is called sufficient; even if he is never going to work it, unless God by efficacious help bring it about, that it be reduced to second act. And thus help sufficient for believing is that, by which man can believe: and help sufficient for persevering that, by which he can persevere if he wills: although that he will will, efficacious help is required besides. Epitome of the helps of divine grace book 3. chap. 17.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIX. As Alvarez observes, aid sufficient for a given operation is of two kinds. One is completely sufficient: beyond it no other aid is absolutely necessary for the operation actually to be produced. The other is not completely sufficient, yet truly sufficient, in that it confers the ability with respect to that operation. No other aid is then absolutely necessary for the person to be truly said to be able to produce it, just as to say that someone can see requires only that he have the power of sight, though many other things beyond that power are needed for him actually to see.

In this sense he maintains that through the aids of the grace which he calls sufficient, a person truly can perform the act in relation to which the grace is called sufficient, even if he will never perform it unless God, by efficacious aid, brings it about that it is reduced to second act. So aid sufficient for believing is aid by which a person can believe, and aid sufficient for persevering is aid by which he can persevere if he wills, though for him actually to will it efficacious aid is further required. Epitome de auxiliis divinae gratiae, book 3, chapter 17.

choices.term: in actu primo ... ad actum secundum
choices.why: Scholastic pair: first act is a power ready to act; second act is the operation itself (XXVII-XXIX).

bible_refs: Diego Alvarez OP (d. 1635), Thomist at the Congregatio de auxiliis; Le Blanc cites an epitome of his De auxiliis divinae gratiae, book 3, chapter 17.
